name: Arnak Fireblade
summary: This errand delivers a recovered cult collar from the shaman Margoz to Arnak Fireblade in Orgrimmar. Margoz suspects the Burning Blade's dark magic requires an experienced warlock to decipher, despite the uneasy truce between the Horde and its practitioners of the occult.

sections.title: A Matter Beyond Shamanism
sections.body: After securing Searing Collars from the Burning Blade cultists entrenched inside Skull Rock, the shaman Margoz finds himself at an impasse. The collars thrum with vile demonic power, an energy fundamentally alien and offensive to the spiritual ways of the shaman. Lacking the specific lore required to identify the source of such foul enchantments, Margoz is forced to seek out an expert whose craft delves into the Nether itself.

sections.title: The Cleft of Shadow
sections.body: To analyze the collar, Margoz points travelers toward Arnak Fireblade, an orc warlock lingering in the subterranean passages of the Cleft of Shadow. In Thrall's Orgrimmar, warlocks operate under a tense, guarded tolerance. Arnak publicly claims his occult studies serve benign purposes and thwart demonkind, but many within the Horde view any manipulation of fel magic with deep suspicion.

faq.q: Why does Margoz send you to a warlock?
faq.answer: Margoz admits that the demonic enchantments bound within the Searing Collars fall completely outside the natural and ancestral purview of shamanism. Divining the origin of fel artifacts requires someone intimately familiar with demonology, forcing him to rely on Arnak Fireblade's occult expertise.
Arnak Fireblade resides deep beneath the red mesas of Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, the shadowy cavern where warlocks and rogue operatives conduct their work away from the general populace.

faq.q: What is Arnak Fireblade's role among the Horde?
faq.answer: Arnak is an orc warlock residing in Orgrimmar. He professes that his occult research is benign and dedicated to countering the threat of demons, though traditionalists across the Horde remain wary of anyone who wields fel power.

faq.q: What happens after Arnak receives the collar?
aliases: what does arnak do with collar
faq.answer: Arnak carefully inspects the searing collar to divine its demonic origin, preparing to unravel which dark master or demon empowered the cultists operating within Durotar.

faq.q: Are warlocks openly accepted in Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Warlocks are permitted in Orgrimmar only on a short leash. Mindful of the catastrophic corruption that nearly destroyed the orcish race, Warchief Thrall restricts their practice to the subterranean Cleft of Shadow, watching them closely to ensure they never serve the Legion.

faq.q: Where did the collar come from?
faq.answer: The collar was recovered from the Burning Blade cultists infesting Skull Rock, a cavern hidden along the northeastern crags of Durotar near the coast.

angles.text: This task highlights the pragmatic necessity of your discipline: when shamans fail against fel arcana, the Horde must turn to the Cleft of Shadow.
Margoz's reluctance to handle the collar underscores the fundamental divide between ancestral elements and the corrupting nature of demonic magic.
Thrall's new society walks a tightrope, tolerating occultists like Arnak in the shadows solely because their dark knowledge is needed to fight demonic cults.
